title: Under the mainsail
note: 3 August 1804. A foggy morning. After breakfast the Oto and Missouria were collected 'under an orning of our Main Sail' at the camp; the party paraded in their presence; the captains made a long speech; the chiefs answered, glad of their 'new fathers'; Big Horse and Hospitality were made second chiefs and four principal men given third-grade medals, Little Thief's medal sent after him; Lewis fired the air gun; and every chief closed by 'asking a little Powder & a Drop of Milk'. The Corps set out at three o'clock and made five miles. Clark named the place Council Bluff and thought it the site for a trading house and a fort. The steps and their odds are the Council rules (scripts/rules/council.gd, data/councils.json).
review: Oto and Missouria presence, speech and dress are placeholders pending the paid cultural review (ADR-0004, ADR-0013). Their words are only what Fairfong and the journals report.

stage.prompt: The chiefs are gathering under the sail

lines.speaker: Sgt. Ordway
lines.text: A foggy morning, Captain. The chiefs are going up to the awning.

lines.speaker: Clark
lines.text: Then let us receive them properly.

choices.label: Parade the Corps under arms
choices.note: Every man turned out in his coat, as the party paraded that morning.

effects.journal: The party paraded in the presence of the Indians.

choices.label: Receive them without ceremony
choices.note: The men keep to their work at the boats.

lines.speaker: Fairfong
lines.text: They are seated, messieurs. Big Horse for the Oto; Hospitality for the Missouria. Little Thief is away on the hunt.

lines.speaker: Fairfong
lines.text: They will hear your words now.

lines.speaker: Clark
lines.text: We will tell them of the change in the government of this country, and what their new father wishes of them.

choices.label: Make the speech
choices.note: It goes through Drouillard and Fairfong into the Oto tongue, if Drouillard is here to carry it.

reply_pass.speaker: Fairfong
reply_pass.text: They say they are glad their new fathers have come, and they will follow the counsel given them.

reply_fail.speaker: Fairfong
reply_fail.text: They have heard you out. They say little. It went through two tongues, messieurs, and lost something in each.

lines.speaker: Clark
lines.text: Now the medals, and the commissions.

choices.label: Make the chiefs: medals in three grades, commissions and a flag
choices.note: Second-grade medals for Big Horse and Hospitality, third for the four principal men.

choices.label: Keep the medals for the nations upriver
choices.note: There are only so many, and the Teton are ahead.

reply_pass.speaker: York
reply_pass.text: Look at them, Captain. They can't make out where the powder goes.

reply_fail.speaker: Fairfong
reply_fail.text: The traders have shown them wonders before.

lines.speaker: Fairfong
lines.text: Every one of them ends the same way, messieurs. A little powder, and a drop of milk.

choices.label: A canister of powder and fifty balls, and a dram all round
choices.note: It wins the day, and arms and drinks away what the Corps must live on.

choices.label: Tell them there is none to spare

lines.speaker: Fairfong
lines.text: And Little Thief? He will hear of this from other mouths if you send him nothing.

choices.label: Send his medal, a flag and the speech after him, with tobacco

lines.speaker: Clark
lines.text: This bluff would make a fine place for a trading house, and a fort. We'll call it Council Bluff.

choices.label: Strike the awning and load the boats

effects.journal: We call this place Council Bluff. Set out at three o'clock.
